topline.text: Sheffield's own review of children suspended or excluded from its schools finds 65% could have been helped earlier, before their needs worsened, and one in five had no support at all beforehand - figures as reported, the underlying committee paper wasn't available to check directly.
That goes to today's education, children & families policy committee alongside a proposed 'alternative curriculum strategy' for earlier intervention, due to start next school year if approved.
topline.action: Worth flagging to MAPs partner schools ahead of next year's rollout.

topline.text: The vote lands amid council turmoil: Sheffield's Labour-Green administration is collapsing over a 'Zionism is racism' motion, with Labour asking Wednesday's full council to let it govern alone - a minority position that could make future decisions, including on this strategy, harder to pass.
Otherwise a quiet 24-48 hours nationally - no major DfE or Ofsted announcements broke overnight.

diary.text: Sheffield's education, children & families policy committee considers the suspensions/SEND review and proposed alternative curriculum strategy.
Sheffield full council votes on Labour's plan to govern alone after the Labour-Green administration's collapse.
Commons Education Committee takes oral evidence from Education Secretary Lucy Powell on the work of the DfE.

items.lede: Suspended repeatedly before help arrived, Sheffield review finds.
items.body: A council review of children suspended or excluded between May and August - drawing on schools, AP providers and families - found 65% could have been supported earlier, before their difficulties deteriorated, and that one in five had received no service beforehand. It goes to today's policy committee alongside a proposed 'alternative curriculum strategy' aimed at earlier intervention, to start next school year if approved. Figures as reported by The Star; flag as unverified against the primary committee paper.
items.action: Worth flagging to MAPs partner schools ahead of the strategy's rollout next year.

items.lede: Council's joint administration set to collapse.
items.body: Sheffield's Labour-Green coalition is breaking up after the Greens refused Labour's ultimatum to disavow a 'Zionism is racism' motion passed at their party conference. Labour leader Fran Belbin will ask Wednesday's full council to let Labour govern alone - a minority position that could make passing decisions, including today's SEND strategy, harder in the months ahead.
